shortDescription: The German day-ahead price was edging down on Monday, as renewables rose, while the German year-ahead contract remained at elevated levels.($1 = 0.8607 euros)

children: The German day-ahead price was edging down on Monday, as renewables rose, while the German year-ahead contract remained at elevated levels.
The German baseload spot electricity contract (TRDEBD1) fell 4.3% to €149.25 ($173.40) per megawatt hour (MWh) at 0743 GMT, LSEG data showed.

Wind power generation was expected to rise by 3.5 gigawatts (GW) to 18.4 GW, while consumption was expected to rise by 1.5 GW to 53.8 GW and solar power is seen roughly stable, edging up by 0.5 GW to close to 15 GW.

"Looking ahead, German wind generation is expected to strengthen further into Tuesday and Wednesday before easing later in the week. Spanish wind should also recover from today's low levels, while French wind remains modest overall," analysts at Engie's Energyscan wrote in a note.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was not traded, according to LSEG data.
Consumption in France was set to rise by around 1 GW to 46.3 GW, while wind power generation was set to rise by a similar figure to 5.3 GW. Solar power generation was set to fall by 1 GW to 4.6 GW.
French nuclear availability rose by two percentage points to 80% of total availability.
Along the curve, Germany's 2027 baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) was up 2.4% to €123/MWh, 0.25 cents away from the three-year high it reached on September 2.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was not traded, according to LSEG data.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was mostly stable, at €84.21 a metric ton.
